title: Vaccines at Work: Experimental Evidence from a Firm Campaign
authors: Manuel Hoffmann; Roberto Mosquera; Adrian Chadi
eligible_reason: Not a staggered DiD. Randomized encouragement field experiment at an Ecuadorian bank: employees were randomly assigned incentives (treatment1/2/4) and an on-site vaccination day (workweek), and the main results are cross-sectional OLS of vaccination take-up and sickness absence on the randomized arms (Tables 2-5), peer-assignment regressions, and an RD on distance (r, c, cXr). The only unit-FE panel regression (Figure A11 and footnote 26: xtreg sick_flu1_ext i.workweek##i.monthc, fe) interacts the time-invariant random assignment with calendar month around a single campaign date, so there is one common treatment date and it is appendix material.
design_notes: Stata; Code/1_data_preparation_cross_section.do, 2_data_preparation_panel.do, 3_analysis.do. Individual-level cross-section plus individual-month health panel (monthc). vce(robust) or cluster unit2.

ineligible_specs_listed.reason: cross-sectional OLS on randomized arms; no adoption timing
randomized workweek assignment x calendar month with individual FE; single common campaign date (not staggered); appendix

data_files_note: README: the bank authorized an anonymized version of the proprietary data; results requiring income (summary stats, RD estimates, some robustness) cannot be replicated. Data/Final is empty and is built by the data-preparation do-files.
data_provenance_note: Anonymized original records with income withheld; no statement of noise or synthesis.
